cohort: 365,056 births at Port Moresby General Hospital in Papua New Guinea between 1977 and 2015
finding: In a low- to middle-income country setting with rapidly increasing birth numbers, a comparatively low perinatal mortality rate can be achieved while maintaining low caesarean section rates through strict use of second-stage protocols, perinatal audit, and supportive training that promotes judicious and proficient use of vacuum extraction and caesarean section.
mod_finding: From 1989 to 2015, the modified mean perinatal mortality rate for vacuum extraction births (98% of which were babies ≥2500 g) was 7.5/1000 births (range 0-21.7; 9.0 in 2015).
